metadata.case_name: LEUNG KWOK BIU v. TAM SAN YU T/A NEW SHINE ENGINEERING CO AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_after: unable to have gainful employment and relied on support by his sons

injuries.description: fracture of cervical C1 (Jefferson Fracture) with associated cord oedema at C1-2 level.
source: he suffered a fracture of cervical C1 (Jefferson Fracture) with associated cord oedema at C1-2 level.
injuries.icd_description: Concussion or oedema of cervical spinal cord

source: he gradually regained consciousness to normal level but was tetraplegic.
He was an incomplete tetraplegia with majority of muscle groups at grade 3/5 power or above.
injuries.icd_description: Other incomplete cord syndrome of cervical spinal cord

manifestations.description: Mild spasticity of all four limbs
Partial sensory impairment of all four limbs
Mild weakness of all four limbs (majority muscle groups at grade 3/5 or above)
Reduced ability to walk (uses walking stick, short distances, wheelchair for longer distances; able to stand for about 30 seconds)
Reduced hand function / partial dependence in eating, grooming, bathing, dressing and toileting (cannot reliably hold chopsticks; partially dependent)
Neurogenic bowel with constipation requiring laxatives and suppositories but without significant stool incontinence
Headache, insomnia, poor concentration and memory deterioration
Major depressive disorder with depressed mood, reduced interest and pleasure, social withdrawal and frequent suicidal ideas (psychiatric sequela)

treatments_future: maintenance psychiatric treatment in the public sector (psychiatrist and clinical psychologist)
periodic physiotherapy and occupational therapy follow-ups

losses.description: Reduced ability to walk and mobilise independently; uses walking stick and wheelchair for outdoor activities; can stand only briefly.
Partial dependence on family for most activities of daily living (e.g. transfers, bathing, dressing, toileting) though modified independence for transfers with aids.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to change clothes, shower, brush teeth, care for hygiene and other self-care without assistance.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Claimed inability to achieve penile erection / erectile dysfunction.
Social withdrawal and staying at home most of the time; loss of previous social activities.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to pursue previous hobbies of photography and Chinese calligraphy.
Deterioration in relationship with wife and children; sense of being a burden and guilt feelings towards family.
Brace scars on his scalp from treatment.
Poor concentration and memory deterioration affecting daily functioning.

comparable_cases.case_name: Lee Suk Yin & Ors v National Insurance Co Ltd representing the estate of Ngai Chung Lit, deceased
comparable_cases.injury_description: Burst fracture of the C6 vertebra, severe head injuries involving loss of consciousness, subdural haematoma and pulmonary contusion; immobilised with halo ring and jacket; hospitalised for 22 months; incomplete tetraplegic and multiple severe deficits; classified in the 'disaster' category.

comparable_cases.case_name: Cham Cheung Sing v Yung Pak Wa & Ors
comparable_cases.injury_description: Serious head and spinal injury leading to tetraplegia; admitted unconscious; permanent paralysis and severe deficits; impairment of whole person assessed at 97%-98%; classified in 'disaster' category.

comparable_cases.case_name: Fung Kwok Ki v Wing Sang Construction Co Ltd
comparable_cases.injury_description: Severe head, neck and chest injuries with tetraplegia; ICU for 20 days; multiple surgeries; partial recovery with permanent residual brain damage and permanent double incontinence; permanent wheelchair dependence.

comparable_cases.case_name: Lai Ping Wah v China Insurance Co Ltd
comparable_cases.injury_description: Passenger thrown from coach, head injury, later developed Devic's Syndrome/multiple sclerosis leading to progressive disability, eventual blindness and tetraplegia; awarded PSLA.
